# Exact parity separation for a differentiable buffered cap problem

This is an abstract lemma for the proposed ACTUAL smoothed H problem.
It is not a claim about ordinary nonsmooth mixed depth. Attainment and
properness must be established for the chosen smoothed objective before
the lemma is applied to it.

Let C be convex, S=C intersect (Z^n x R^d), and f:C->R be concave.
Fix epsilon>=0. For N=(a,u), u nonzero, write G(u)>0 and let

    F_N(b)=sum_z integral_(C_z)
        Psi((a.z+u.x-b)/(delta G(u))) dx,

where delta>0 and Psi is a C^1 nondecreasing function. Assume all
integrals and their derivatives below exist (bounded C and a bounded
compactly supported Psi' suffice). A cap at Y=(p,y) uses threshold

    b_N(Y)=a.p+u.y-epsilon f(Y)G(u).

Define its depth as the infimum of F_N(b_N(Y)), with any additional
vertical caps allowed. Let Q be the attained maximum depth on S.
Assume that at every deepest point a finite nonvertical normal attains
the infimum and its smoothed section mass

    T_N(b)=sum_z integral_(C_z)
           Psi'((a.z+u.x-b)/(delta G(u)))/(delta G(u)) dx

is strictly positive at the attaining threshold. Pure base-normal
variations are unrestricted; f(Y), delta, and G(u) do not depend on a.

## Lemma

Distinct deepest bases have distinct integer parities. In particular
there are at most 2^n deepest bases. If f is strictly concave within
each positive-dimensional fiber and epsilon>0, there is also at most
one deepest point per base.

## Proof

Suppose deepest points Y_0=(p_0,y_0), Y_1=(p_1,y_1) have equal base
parity. Their midpoint Y_m belongs to S. For any fixed N, concavity
of f gives

    b_N(Y_m)<=(b_N(Y_0)+b_N(Y_1))/2.

Since F_N is nonincreasing, its superlevel in the threshold variable
is an interval. Both endpoint depths are Q, so every fixed cap has
mass at least Q there. The displayed inequality gives mass at least
Q at Y_m for each normal. Vertical caps have the same elementary
convex-superlevel property. Thus Y_m is deepest as well.

Choose an attaining nonvertical N at Y_m and put q=b_N(Y_m), so
F_N(q)=Q. Positivity of T_N(q) implies strict decrease in a
neighborhood of q. Monotonicity then implies F_N(b)<Q for EVERY b>q.
The two endpoint cap masses are at least Q, so b_N(Y_i)<=q.
Combining with midpoint concavity gives

    q<=(b_N(Y_0)+b_N(Y_1))/2<=q.

Hence both endpoint thresholds equal q. The very SAME cap normal and
threshold therefore attain the depth at Y_0 and at Y_1.

At an endpoint source p_i, differentiate its cap mass with respect to
the unrestricted base normal a. Since the normal is a minimum, its
gradient vanishes:

    0=sum_z integral_(C_z) (z-p_i)
       Psi'((a.z+u.x-q)/(delta G(u)))/(delta G(u)) dx.

The measure in this equation is the same at both endpoints and has
positive mass T_N(q). Its base centroid must equal both p_0 and p_1.
Thus p_0=p_1. This proves parity separation of distinct bases.

If the two marks share a base but have different continuous
coordinates, strict own-fiber concavity of f and epsilon>0 would
make the midpoint threshold inequality strict, contradicting the
threshold equalities already obtained. This proves the last assertion.

No halfspace is dropped, no continuous base is rounded, and no claim
is made that a selected auxiliary centroid lies in S. The integer
midpoint is an actual feasible point by parity and convexity.

## Scope for the new H program

Once the outward-kernel smoothed objective has actual attainment,
uniform proper source marks, and a positive own smoothed section, the
lemma makes every positive-width deepest group a SINGLE point.
The original occupied-face homothety and facet cases then need not be
imported into that different variational problem. The exact sharp
Gamma_d/2^n numerical payment is still required.
